Share on X Telegram Ayima Lott-Jonathan, wife of former President Goodluck Jonathan, is set to unveil a memoir detailing her personal experiences and life journey as she marks her 50th birthday.
According to a report by The Cable, the memoir, titled ‘Gold Dust: Treasures of Quiet Years’, is scheduled for public presentation in Abuja on November 19.
Lott-Jonathan, who largely maintained a low public profile during her husband’s tenure as president, uses the 12-chapter book to reflect on her life, with particular attention to her experiences in the Niger Delta and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
The event is expected to attract prominent political figures, traditional rulers and other dignitaries.
Former Vice-President Namadi Sambo is expected to chair the occasion, while Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, will serve as the chief book presenter.
Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, will be the chief host and one of the book presenters, alongside Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, who will serve as co-presenter.
The chairman of the Bayelsa State Council of Traditional Rulers, Bubaraye Agada IV, will serve as the royal father of the day and lead other first-class traditional rulers to the event.
Former President Goodluck Jonathan is also expected to attend as the chief special guest of honour.
The memoir will be reviewed by Professor G.G. Darah, a scholar of folklore and oral literature, Fellow of the Nigerian Academy of Letters and former chairman of the editorial board of The Guardian newspaper.
Born with an interest in law and education, Lott-Jonathan studied law at the Rivers State University of Science and Technology and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2003.
She subsequently pursued further studies in educational leadership and administration, earning qualifications from the National Teachers’ Institute, Nigeria, as well as master’s and doctoral degrees from Walden University in the United States.
In 2008, she established Aduvie International School in Abuja, marking her entry into the education sector.
According to the organisers, Gold Dust: Treasures of Quiet Years explores themes of patience, determination, courage, motherhood and purposeful service.
The book also offers reflections on faith, navigating bereavement and dealing with delayed fulfilment, drawing from the author’s personal experiences.
The organisers said the memoir is intended to inspire readers, particularly younger generations, by highlighting the importance of resilience, perseverance and remaining committed to one’s purpose despite life’s challenges.
